Episode 243: The Surprise Attack of the Red King (3)
On April 25, 1804, one day had passed since the Jukmyeong people ambushed Drakka.

The entire world already knew that Drakka had fallen. The fact that Kelriak had fled without even putting up a proper fight, and that the Jukmyeong people had conquered Drakka without suffering any damage.
It was not an exaggeration to describe it as the biggest shock since the dawn of history.

It was more shocking than when the King of Chaos appeared at Geomhwa Castle, more than when the demon was born in the Garden of Swords, and even more than shortly before the demonic world led by Demon King Jito invaded the human world. People were engulfed in greater shock.
As saints, they could only think that Jipul had "collapsed." Shimat described the real heart of Jipul as the Tower of Stories, but the federation's capital was undoubtedly Drakka.
“The guys who sounded the alarm in Meisil, they attacked Jipul so soon...... and they've even taken over Drakka?”
Tikan.
Luna placed a bundle of newsletters on the conference room table and spoke. News outlets worldwide were incessantly releasing special reports.

The Bamel Union, led by Dino Jaglun, was also publishing articles. These were not reports on the damage situation in the Lutero Federation. They mainly consisted of various information for the refugees coming from the federation to the union and content to reassure the current residents.
“Nari! Please look at this. These are newsletters just released by Jipul's media.”
Jet entered the conference room, holding up the newsletters. They were from the media that had long served as Jipul's pen in the battle for public opinion.
(A long-standing ruler has set, and a red sun has risen.
Despite a battle so large that Drakka fell, nowhere in the city or nearby autonomous districts were those in mourning easy to find.

Surprisingly, civilians were not harmed in this battle at all. The Jukmyeong people kept the promise they made to the citizens when declaring war, and Jipul left Drakka, suffering near-total destruction.
Drakka's evolution began immediately after the war ended.
The Jukmyeong people, based on their superior technology, instantly replaced all the buildings and institutions that had been destroyed during the battle.

Long-range communication devices, which had been used only by the Bamel Union, were deployed throughout the city, and devices to replace the moving portals that had been unusable since the aftermath of the demonic incident appeared, and so on......)
"Wow, these disloyal brats. After all they've taken from Jipul, they're spreading news bad-mouthing Jipul like this?"
Veradin said, clicking his tongue.
After Drakka fell, he felt confused and strange emotions. Although his mind was ill and he had no good memories from his time as a noble in Jipul, Jipul was still his foundation and homeland.
Of course, Veradin is now a member of the Bamel Union and knows better than anyone the disgusting and rotten internal affairs of Jipul.
"Does Lord Veradin still have affection for Jipul!?" Enya said.
"No, that was just a joke. I want Jipul to fall too. But I didn't expect it to go in this direction. They should atone and contribute to the world and society, then collapse."
"You know better than anyone that Jipul won't fall from this, Veradin."
At Jin's words, Veradin nodded.

"That's true, but... this is really weird. A day has passed and Jipul is not making any attempt to recover Drakka. They're focusing on defending the Tower of Stories. I'm worried that Kelriak, that monstrous author, might do something that crosses the line in this process."
It was a plausible story.
He might become more obsessed with the Mage Stone in connection with Ganestogawa, or suddenly complete the Mage Stone in the process.
Veradin was afraid of that. The moment the Mage Stone is completed, the land and soldiers that Jipul lost this time will not be a loss.
"If it's crossing the line, it would only be about the Mage Stone. Conversely, that means that Kelriak is nothing if he cannot complete the Mage Stone. So don't worry too much, Veradin."
Mage Stone.
Lately, Jin had been thinking that the completion of the Mage Stone might depend on Elona.

The core of the Mage Stone from a thousand years ago, which manipulated history entirely, confirmed in Temaru's tombs, was undoubtedly Elona. Jipul had done the most damage to reality and history when she directly controlled the Tower of Stories.
'However, the image of Elona confirmed in the tombs' subspaces was definitely not using the Holy Water Vessel, as now. She looked like an ordinary human, like the first time I saw Lady Elona.'
Jin had never seen Elona using the Holy Water Vessel from the recording device.
Although it's true that she became stronger using the Holy Water Vessel, she is no longer a human with will, but just a terrible weapon of war.
"Veradin, you remember during your time in the province that the Tower of Tales communicated with Lady Elona, right?"
"Right."
"Then, can the now soulless Lady Elona properly communicate with the Tower of Tales?"
Veradin's eyes widened; this was a realm he hadn't considered.

"Probably not. So, if my prediction is correct, the Holy Crown will be a great power to Kelliac but also a constraint. If she can't communicate with the tower, she can't properly use the Magician's Stone, and if the control of the Holy Crown is released, Lady Elona won't obediently listen to him."
"It really could be that way. If Kelliac tries to solve that problem and asks for help... the immediate things that come to mind are the Sun Cult, Kinzelo, and maybe Ganesto."
"But the Sun Cult has completely severed its relationship with Gipil after the battle of Meisil. It must be Kinzelo or Ganesto. The latter is more likely since they are already collaborating."
They hadn't received much additional information about them. Kinzelo seemed to be lying low, and the Bamal Alliance was wary of their dream capabilities.
They were tracking the recently discovered 'World of Rokia' through record magic. But there wasn't much income.

"With Drakka fallen, Ganesto will soon make a move to aid Kelliac. We'll have to track them more diligently then. Even if they don't move, it's not necessarily bad. It means their relationship is not as good as we think."

Among the enemies, the aliens were the ones the Alliance had to worry about the most at the moment. Their war capabilities, revealed so far, were at a level where they could strike the entire continent at any time.
"Drakka was suddenly attacked from underground, but... even if they had invaded in a more conventional way, it would have been hard to withstand."
There were only two areas in the world that could rival Drakka's defense.
The Garden of Swords, and Tichan.
Those two areas could show even stronger defense than Drakka under specific circumstances, when Jin and Murakan, and the other superhumans of the Alliance, were all on standby.
So, from now on, the Alliance needed to keep more superhuman-level personnel on standby than before.

The aliens could appear anywhere over Alliance territory, leading air fortresses and crossing dimensional gates. Except for Ganesto, they had the perfect right of preemptive strike against all forces.

"We'll have to reduce the number of personnel going on external missions... The good thing is, since the Jitoga finale, the cracks that opened everywhere in the world have disappeared, so civilian casualties won't increase for now, unless the aliens attack."
"Hmm!"
Suddenly, Elliot cleared his throat, and everyone's attention turned to him.
"Master?"
Luna had become accustomed to calling him "Master" before she knew it. She didn't completely trust him as a master yet, but the idea of being someone's disciple didn't seem so bad either.
"You guys don't know Shimat well. But I know him better than anyone else."
"What do you mean?"
"He doesn't like adventure. Like the recent Drakka battle, he enjoys fighting only when he knows he can win perfectly."
Eltieth locked eyes with Jin.
"Therefore, if Shimat attacks the Garden of Swords or Tikan, it will be when you and your guardian dragon, along with my disciples and most other superhumans, are absent."
"That's what Jin was saying."

"It's different, my disciple. You can't always be on standby with your top forces, can you? Suppose the Ganestos suddenly appear one day, and to catch them, both Jin and Murakan have to be out. Would the enemy tribe just stand by and watch?"
"So, Commander Eltieth, you have a contingency plan?"
Out of respect for Luna's master Eltieth, Jin used polite language. It felt awkward to use informal language when Luna was speaking respectfully.

"Of course, isn't it obvious? I've noticed that your alliance has a fairly useful warship. It's called the Golden Ship? It may seem a bit inferior compared to the air fortress, but you can mass-produce it."
"It's not that we didn't want to mass-produce it, Master."

"Bang! You think I didn't know that? My disciple, your master is not merely physically gifted like you. Our Cheongmyeong tribe might be slightly inferior to the enemy tribe, but we had a splendid civilization and technology incomparable to this era."
Jin's eyes widened.
"Oh ... Commander Eltieth, you mean you can reproduce the technology used in those days?"

"Exactly. Before I became a divine warrior, I was one of the top technicians of the Cheongmyeong tribe. However, since my memory isn't entirely intact, I'll need some preparation to recall the knowledge of that time."
"Preparations?"

"Yes, preparations. Just looking at the news that Jet brought, they've already placed the enemy tribe's stuff as public facilities all over Drakka. Besides, Shimat must have taken over most of the nearby autonomous districts, cities, and key points of the existing Lutero Federation by now. He probably installed ancient high-tech equipment in those cities as well. Shimat seems to want to play the good ruler."
Eltieth paused and smiled slyly.

"Let's go and get those things, my disciple. If I dismantle them one by one and study them, my memory will return. You can fight and deal with the enemy tribe as part of your training and also gain knowledge. How clever is that?"
